title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook (2027)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standardized practices for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, interviewers, and people managers. Use the templates and checklists linked below for operational execution.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors with expected duration > 6 months, and roles hired into Redwood’s core product and platform teams.
- Excludes short-term contractors, interns (see intern onboarding playbook), and acquisitions (see M&A integration checklist).

1) Hiring process (Standard operating procedure)
Purpose: hire high-quality candidates quickly while maintaining fairness, diversity, and compliance.
Owner: hiring manager + people-ops recruiter.

High-level stages:
1. Job requisition & approval
   - Manager completes job requisition form (JD template) and justification.
   - People-ops reviews budget and headcount within 3 business days.
   - Approval gate: hiring exec or finance sign-off for senior roles (L5+) or market adjustments.
2. Sourcing & screening
   - Recruiter sources via inbound candidates, referrals, marketplace, and targeted outreach.
   - Initial screen (30 min) completed within 7 calendar days of requisition approval.
   - Screening checklist: role fit, compensation expectations, notice period, right-to-work verification basics.
3. Interview loop
   - Standard panel: 4 interviews (technical/role, system design or case study, behavioral/culture, manager match).
   - Typical timeline: schedule interviews within 7 business days of passing screen; panel completes loop within 10 business days.
   - Interviewers must use the official scorecard and provide written notes within 24 hours.
   - DEI guidance: include at least one interviewer trained in inclusive interviewing for all external hires.
4. Decision & calibration
   - Hiring manager collates scorecards and recommends hire/decline.
   - People-ops runs a calibration check for senior hires or when compensation exceeds band midpoint.
5. Offer & negotiation
   - Recruiter prepares offer packet with base salary, equity, target bonus (if applicable), and standard benefits summary.
   - Standard SLA: extend verbal offer within 5 business days of decision.
   - Offer must be approved by compensation partner for any exceptions to band or sign-on.
6. Background checks & preboarding
   - Conditional offer sent subject to background checks and reference checks (completed prior to start date).
   - Recruiter initiates preboarding tasks and assigns a buddy.

Interview and scorecard standards:
- Scorecard sections: technical skills (0-5), role competencies (0-5), communication (0-5), cultural fit (0-5), overall recommendation (hire/hold/no-hire).
- Interviewers document specific evidence for each score and cite examples.
- Conflict-of-interest rule: interviewers who referred the candidate should not be the sole approvers.

Hiring SLAs and metrics (target):
- Time-to-fill (requisition approval -> accepted offer): 35 days median.
- Time-to-hire (initial screen -> accepted offer): 21 days median.
- Offer acceptance rate target: >= 80% for engineering roles.
- Diversity sourcing: at least 30% of slate from underrepresented groups for senior roles.

2) New hire onboarding (First 90 days)
Purpose: accelerate new hire time-to-productivity and ensure policy and security compliance.
Owner: people-ops + hiring manager + IT.

Preboarding (before Day 1)
- Send welcome email with start logistics, first-day agenda, and handbook link.
- IT creates accounts and provisions equipment at least 3 business days before start.
- Manager prepares 30-60-90 plan and shares with new hire.
- Assign buddy and schedule first-week 1:1s.

Day 1 checklist
- People-ops: welcome meeting, company overview, benefits enrollment walkthrough.
- IT: equipment handoff, MFA setup, access to Slack, SSO, and core internal services.
- Manager: team intro, role goals, and immediate priorities.

Week 1-4 (onboarding program)
- Role onboarding sessions: codebase walkthrough, architecture overview, product demos, and key contacts.
- Mandatory trainings: security, data handling, and compliance modules; complete by end of week 2.
- Buddy check-ins: daily first week, then weekly until week 8.

30-60-90 plan (example objectives)
- 30 days: understand codebase and developer workflow, complete 1 small bug fix or doc change, meet cross-functional partners.
- 60 days: land first feature or deliverable with code review, present onboarding learnings to team.
- 90 days: operate independently on standard tasks, propose one improvement to onboarding or product.

Access & security
- Required completion: SSO, MFA, security training, acceptable use policy signature before production access.
- Least privilege principle: production credentials are gated and require manager+security approval.

Onboarding success metrics
- New hire happiness (first 30 days survey) target >= 4/5.
- Ramp time (time to first independent deliverable) median target 60 days for IC roles.

3) Performance & feedback cycles
Purpose: establish clear expectations, frequent feedback, and equitable evaluation.
Owner: manager + people-ops (calibration & compensation).

Cadence and calendar
- Continuous feedback: managers are expected to give regular informal feedback during 1:1s and code reviews.
- Formal cycles:
  - Mid-year check-in (June): progress against goals, development planning.
  - Year-end performance review (December): ratings, calibration, and compensation recommendations.
  - Compensation adjustment cycle (January fiscal process): salary changes and bonus payouts.

Goal setting and OKRs
- Each team sets 3-5 quarterly goals; individual goals should map to team objectives.
- SMART goal guidance: specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound.

Performance rating and calibration
- Rating scale: Exceeds Expectations / Meets Expectations / Needs Improvement.
- Calibration process: managers submit ratings and evidence; people-ops convenes calibration panels by function to ensure consistency and equity.
- Calibration inputs: peer feedback, customer impact, quantitative metrics (uptime, latency improvements where applicable), and code contributions.

Career development & promotion paths
- Promotion decisions require manager recommendation, peer feedback, and manager+director sign-off.
- Promotion criteria documented per IC/Manager ladders; see linked promotion rubric templates.

Performance improvement (PIP)
- Trigger: repeated Needs Improvement rating or significant performance gaps.
- PIP essentials: clear objectives, success criteria, weekly checkpoints, and a 60- to 90-day timeline.
- Ownership: manager owns PIP implementation; people-ops reviews for fairness and legal alignment.

4) Manager playbook (day-to-day responsibilities)
Hiring & onboarding
- Partner with recruiter on role profile, interview panel, and scorecards.
- Set 30-60-90 plan and meet daily in week 1.

1:1s and feedback
- 1:1 cadence: weekly for direct reports (30-60 min).
- Suggested 1:1 structure: quick personal check-in, progress on priorities, blockers, career discussion, and action items.
- Document decisions and action items in shared notes.

Career growth & coaching
- Conduct quarterly career conversations; maintain development plans for each direct report.
- Provide stretch projects and cross-team exposure.

Compensation & recognition
- Recommend compensation changes supported by evidence; route exceptions to compensation partner.
- Use public recognition channels for team wins and peer nominations.

Difficult conversations
- Use clear examples and documented evidence.
- For behavioral or ethical concerns, escalate to people-ops and security as needed.

5) Policies & practical details
Working model
- Hybrid default: 3 days in office for engineers; managers set team-specific schedules within the hybrid policy.
- Remote-first exceptions require manager+people-ops approval for permanent remote.

Time off & leave
- PTO accrual: standard policy document linked in Resources.
- Parental leave: primary caregiver 16 weeks paid; secondary caregiver 6 weeks paid (subject to local law).

Equipment & expenses
- Standard issue laptop and monitor allocation; managers submit requests to IT four weeks before start for new hires.
- Expense reimbursements follow financial policy; submit within 60 days.

6) Templates, checklists and links
- Job description template: /confluence/templates/job-description.json (use JD template for consistent role profiles).
- Interview scorecard template: /confluence/templates/interview-scorecard.md.
- 30-60-90 plan template: /confluence/templates/30-60-90-plan.md.
- New hire checklist (printable): /confluence/templates/onboarding-checklist.pdf.

7) Roles & responsibilities (summary)
- Hiring manager: role definition, interviewing, decision, onboarding ownership.
- Recruiter: sourcing, candidate coordination, offer administration.
- People-ops: policy oversight, calibration facilitation, records, and compliance.
- IT/Security: account provisioning, access controls, device lifecycle.

8) Frequently asked questions
Q: Who creates the offer letter?
A: The recruiter drafts the offer; compensation partner approves band exceptions.

Q: What if an interviewer misses a debrief?
A: Interviewers must submit their scorecard within 24 hours. If unavailable, the hiring manager documents the reason and proceeds with at least two other panel inputs.

Q: How are promotions handled mid-year?
A: Promotions are allowed outside the annual cycle with manager+director approval and compensation partner sign-off.

9) Revision history
- 2026-12-15: Created (Aisha Patel)
- 2027-02-10: Updated interview SLAs, onboarding checklist, and promotion guidance (reviewers: Sofia Martinez, Ravi Kapoor, Emma Liu).

Related resources and templates are stored in the People Ops Confluence space. For questions or suggested updates, contact people-ops@redwood.ai or open an edit request via the Confluence edit flow.
